messages:
olivia: Heads-up — spotted inconsistent Request-ID examples in /api/v1/generate docs. curl shows `X-Request-Id`, python snippet uses `request-id`, and Go example omits it. Also the response schema examples show `request_id` in some places and `requestId` in others. This will confuse users and break webhooks.

tj: Can you paste the exact snippets or point to the PR?

olivia: PR is https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482, commit 8a3c7f2. Example currently in the markdown:```
curl -H 'request-id: abc123' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
That should be `X-Request-Id: abc123`. Also OpenAPI examples render `request_id` (snake_case) in the response example, but runtime returns `requestId` (camelCase).

chris: Backend check: nginx/proxy sets the header as `X-Request-Id` and our app populates a `requestId` field in JSON responses. So the canonical header is `X-Request-Id` and canonical JSON key is `requestId`.

maya: For SDKs, header names are effectively case-insensitive, but common examples use `X-Request-Id`. I suggest we standardize examples to `X-Request-Id` (Title-Case) and add a note "headers are case-insensitive". For response JSON, prefer `requestId` in code/documentation.

sam: I'll take the PR. Plan: update curl/python/go snippets, fix the OpenAPI example to use `requestId`, and add a short migration note for consumers who expect `request_id`. Also add a unit check so future changes don't regress examples.

docs-bot: PR 482 preview build: https://deploy-preview-482.docs.redwood.ai — no broken links reported. :white_check_mark:

tj: Also check the TypeScript/TS types and Go client types — I saw a `request_id` in the generated type defs. @maya can you update the codegen template so generated clients use `requestId`?

maya: Yep — updating the generator template now. Will push a small change to codegen and attach the sample diff here. Should be backwards-safe (we'll map old snake_case to camelCase where we can).

sam: Proposed inline fixes to include in the PR:```
# curl
curl -H 'X-Request-Id: abc123' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

# python
import requests
headers = {'X-Request-Id': 'abc123'}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers=headers, json={...})

# go
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", body)
req.Header.Set("X-Request-Id", "abc123")
```
And replace the JSON response example with:```json
{
  "requestId": "abc123",
  "id": "r_12345",
  "object": "response",
  "choices": [...]
}
```

olivia: Thank you. Small request — add a one-liner in the migration guide: "If you relied on snake_case `request_id`, update consumers to `requestId` (camelCase) and treat the header as case-insensitive."

tj: Agreed. Sam, can you merge once CI passes? Aim for the noon docs deploy window.

sam: On it — I'll add a test that compares the published examples to the canonical snippet in /specs/examples/request-id.md so we catch future drift. Merging after green CI.

docs-bot: PR 482 merged by sam at 3098765450. :tada: 

olivia: Awesome — thanks everyone, especially @maya for the codegen patch and @sam for the quick PR turnaround. I'll follow up if any downstream customers report issues.
